text: Better [is] a dry morsel and quietness with it, than a house full of feasting with strife.
A wise servant rules over a son who acts shamefully, and in the midst of brothers he will share an inheritance.
The crucible [is] for silver and the furnace for gold, and the One testing hearts [is] YHWH.
One doing evil pays attention to lips of iniquity; a liar gives ear to a tongue of evil desires.
One mocking the poor scorns his Maker; one glad at calamity will not be acquitted.
The crown of old men [are] the sons of sons, and the glory of sons [are] their fathers.
A lip of excellence is not lovely to a fool, even less to a prince [is] a lip of falsehood.
A stone of favor [is] a bribe in the eyes of its owners—to all that he turns, he prospers.
The one covering a transgression is seeking love, and one repeating a word is separating a close friend.
A rebuke goes down into an understanding one, more than a hundred stripes into a fool.
An evil one seeks only rebellion, and a cruel messenger will be sent against him.
Let meet a bear robbed of her cubs with a man, and not a fool in his folly.
One returning evil in exchange for good—evil shall not depart from his house.
The beginning of strife [is] a letting out of waters, and before it breaks out, abandon the dispute.
One justifying the wicked, and condemning the just—even the two of them [are] an abomination to YHWH.
Why [is] [is] this a payment in the hand of a fool, to buy wisdom without a heart?
At every time a friend is loving, and a brother is born for distress.
A man lacking heart is one striking hands, pledging a pledge before the face of his friend.
The one loving transgression loves strife; the one making high his entrance is seeking destruction.
The twisted of heart shall not find good, and the turned in his tongue falls into evil.
The one begetting a fool, grief [is] unto him, and the father of a fool is not glad.
A joyful heart is good healing, and a spirit stricken dries up the bones.
A wicked one takes a bribe from the bosom to stretch aside the paths of justice.
With the face of a discerning one [is] wisdom and the eyes of a fool [are] at the end of the earth.
A foolish son [is] a grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.
Surely to fine the righteous [is] not good, to strike nobles for uprightness.
The one restraining his words [is] one knowing knowledge, [and] calm of spirit [is] a man of understanding.
Even a fool keeping silent is considered wise, one shutting his lips discerning.
